title: Meeting the smith, remembering the iron
odia:
ବାଟରେ ଦେଖିଲି କମାର
ଲୁହା ପଜାଇଦେ ଆମର।
literal_meaning: I saw a blacksmith on the road: sharpen our iron [implement].
meaning_odia: ବାଟରେ କମାରଙ୍କୁ ଦେଖିବାମାତ୍ରେ ଆମ ଲୁହା ପଜାଇଦିଅ ବୋଲି ଅନୁରୋଧ ଆସୁଛି। ପଜାଇବା ମାନେ ଧାର କରିବା; କେଉଁ ଲୁହା ଉପକରଣ ତାହା କୁହାଯାଇନାହିଁ। ଆମ ପାଠରେ ଅଚାନକ ମିଳିଥିବା ସୁଯୋଗକୁ ନିଜ କାମ ସହ ଯୋଡ଼ିବାର ଚିତ୍ର ଏହା। କାମଟି ହେଲା କି ନାହିଁ, ପଙ୍କ୍ତି ସେ କଥା କହୁନାହିଁ।
explanation: An encounter immediately becomes a request for useful work. Our editorial reading notices the quick move from recognising someone’s skill to asking for one’s own task to be done. Depending on the setting, it can sound resourceful or opportunistic; the verse does not say whether the smith accepts.
usage_example: Original imagined example: Someone meets a friend who repairs bicycles and immediately remembers a wheel needing attention. Another person teases them with the blacksmith-on-the-road saying.
cultural_context: The rhyme links କମାର and ଆମର, the worker encountered and the speaker’s own possession. The change from “I saw” to a direct request compresses the whole encounter into two lines.
